### 1 · The intelligence loop and value creation in the age of AI agents

| | |
|---|---|
| **📰 Journal** | Strategic Entrepreneurship Journal (SEJ) |
| **👤 Authors** | Yong Li · Ming Zeng · Alexis Li |
| **📅 Published** | 2026-10-30 |
| **🏷️ Tags** | `FT50` `Innovation-Core` `Open Access` |
| **🔗 DOI** | [10.1002/sej.70067](https://doi.org/10.1002/sej.70067) |

**Abstract** — Abstract Research Summary Artificial intelligence (AI) is moving from generating outputs to executing work. An agent that executes work autonomously produces something generative AI does not: operational experience that can raise its future intelligence. Prior research on AI emphasizes value creation through demand‐side feedback, notably data network effects, in which user data improve prediction and reinforce adoption. We develop the supply‐side counterpart, the intelligence loop: delegated usage generates operational experience, agentic capability converts it into future intelligence, and the resulting value maintains or expands usage. The loop cannot operate until autonomous execution is viable, a threshold we call minimum viable intelligence (MVI). Crossing MVI does not guarantee risin...

**Topics:** `Artificial Intelligence Applications` `Digital Platforms and Economics` `Business Strategies and Innovation`

### 2 · The Future of Entrepreneurship Research Includes Online Panel Data—If Used Correctly

|---|---|
| **📰 Journal** | Entrepreneurship Theory and Practice (ETP) |

| **🔗 DOI** | [10.1177/10422587261496321](https://doi.org/10.1177/10422587261496321) |

**Abstract** — As online panel data (OPD) become more widely used across the behavioral sciences, editors, reviewers, and researchers in entrepreneurship are asking whether it has a legitimate place in our field. We believe the answer is yes—provided three conditions are met. First, the online panel’s participants and definition of entrepreneur must match the research question. Second, studies must incorporate best practices for sample verification. Third, generalizability must be explicitly addressed as part of the study (or set of studies). If researchers do these things, OPD can meaningfully advance both theory and practice in entrepreneurship research. That said, real questions remain. What kinds of studies are suitable for OPD? **Abstract** — Abstract Research Summary Despite the growing use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in entrepreneurship, research on its impact remains fragmented. To address this limitation, we provide an integrative, entrepreneur‐centered review of how GenAI influences entrepreneurs at each stage of the entrepreneurial process: (1) opportunity recognition and ideation, (2) opportunity evaluation and commitment, (3) resource assembly and mobilization, and (4) venture launch and growth. Based on our review, we propose the Empowerment–Entrapment Framework, which not only catalogs GenAI's benefits and costs throughout the entrepreneurial process but also identifies potential trade‐offs underlying GenAI's double‐edged role. Contraction inflexibility determines leverage more than expansion inflexibility. Moreover, inflexibility explains financial leverage on top of operating leverage variability and cash flow variability. **Abstract** — Abstract I propose a mechanism through which institutional investors’ correlated demand shocks provide a source of market risk in asset pricing. Institutional investors have mandates to beat a similar market index. This incentive induces procyclical risk-taking behavior, generating correlated demand that elevates the market betas and risk premia of exposed stocks.
